Schedule A

By-Law
No. 2870/85

Whereas
the Municipal Government Act empowers the City of Red Deer to
regulate and control by By-law the days and hours during which businesses are
required to close;

And
Whereas
the Council of the City of Red Deer wishes to
restrict the hours of business within the City of Red Deer in order that
commercial activity might be confined within reasonable limits;

And
Whereas
the Council of the City of Red Deer wishes to
ensure that at least one day in the week remains substantially free of
commercial activities so that the citizens of Red Deer might benefit thereby
and be permitted to engage in family, social, recreational and other activities
so as to enhance the quality of life and to generally promote the health and
welfare of the citizens in the City of Red Deer;

And
Whereas
the Council of the City of Red Deer wishes to
enact a By-law consistent with and not contrary to the rights and freedoms
guaranteed every Canadian by the
Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms
;

And
Whereas
the Council of the City of Red Deer declares
the object of this By-law to be secular in nature as stated above;

Now
Therefore The Council Of The City Of Red Deer, In The Province Of Alberta, Duly
Assembled, Enacts As Follows:

1. This By-law may be referred to as the
“Hours of Business By-law”.

2. In this By-law,

(
a
) “Area of Business Establishment”
means the area of the business establishment as calculated for business tax
purposes and as recorded in the records of the City Assessor. Where no such
record is kept, area shall mean the total area of the business establishment as
the same would be calculated for business tax purposes.

(
b
) “Business” means the selling of
goods or services for consumption or use and not for resale and includes the
selling of goods or services by hawkers, pedlars and transient traders.

(
c
) “Business Establishment”,
“establishment”, “premises”, “shop”, or “store”, in the appropriate case, means
the premises, building, booth, stall or place where a business is carried on
and includes any booth, stall or place where goods are exposed or offered for
sale or by public auction.

(
d
) “Person” includes a natural
person, a partnership, a corporation and any of their officers, agents or
employees.

(
d.
1) “Convenience Store” means a
business establishment which sells only miscellaneous food and grocery items,
dairy products, books, magazines, newspapers, cigarettes, candy, snack food and
a selection of miscellaneous items.

(
e
) “Sell” or “selling”, “sale”,
“sold”, “sales”, in the appropriate case includes offering for sale or
attempting to sell or barter directly or indirectly on any pretense or by any
device whatsoever.

3. No person shall conduct business in the
City of Red Deer between the hours of 12:00 p.m. and 6:00 a.m. on any day of
the week.

4. On a Sunday, no person shall conduct
business or admit members of the public to a business establishment in the City
of Red Deer unless during any period of 24 consecutive hours in the 6 days
immediately following the Sunday the premises are closed to the public and no
goods or services are sold to the public.

5. No person shall conduct business or
admit members of the public to a business establishment in the City of Red Deer
between the hours of 9.00 o’clock in the forenoon and 12 o’clock noon on the 11th
day of November in any year.

6. Sections 3 and 4 do not apply to a
convenience store where the total area of the business establishment is less
than 3000 square feet.

7. Section 4 does not apply to a business
establishment containing a pharmacy within the meaning of the Pharmaceutical
Association Act where the total area of the business establishment is less than
3000 square feet.

8. Section 4 does not apply where the only
goods offered or available for sale are:

(
a
) potted plants and accessory
supplies, flowers and floral arrangements, horticultural supplies, bedding
plants, nursery stock, and in conjunction therewith, accessory gardening and
lawn care supplies but not including garden and lawn equipment;

(
b
) those goods that are available
for sale at a greenhouse, Market Garden or householders garage sale; or

(
c
) handicrafts.

9. Sections 3 and 4 do not apply where the
only goods offered or available for sale are fuels (gasoline, diesel, propane,
etc.), motor oil and lubricants, or related goods or services for consumption,
maintenance or use in the operation of motor vehicles, motorized equipment,
boats or aircraft.

10. Sections 3 and 4 do not apply in
respect of charging the public admission to premises for live and cinematic
productions, exhibits and facilities for educational, recreational, cultural or
amusement purposes or in respect of the sale or offering for sale of goods or
services incidental to those purposes.

11. Section 4 does not apply to a grocery
store, groceteria or food store of an area of 18000 square feet or less.

12. Sections 3 and 4 do not apply to a taxi
business, hotel, motel or restaurant.

13. This By-law does not apply to the
activities of any public facility operated under the authority of the City of
Red Deer or of a School Board or Community Center in the City of Red Deer, or
to any activity otherwise authorized by law.

14. Any person who contravenes Section 3 or
4 of this By-law is guilty of an offence and shall be liable upon conviction to
a penalty not exceeding $1,000.00 plus costs, and in default of payment to
imprisonment for up to 60 days.

15. Any person who contravenes Section 5 of
this By-law is liable on summary conviction on a first offence to a minimum
fine of $1,000.00 and a maximum fine of $2,000.00; on a second offence to a
minimum fine of $2,000.00 and a maximum fine of $5,000.00; on a third offence
to a minimum fine of $5,000.00 and a maximum fine of $10,000.00. In addition to
a fine the Court may, in each case direct payment of costs and direct that in
default of payment of the fine, the person be imprisoned for a period not
exceeding 6 months.

16. Every person who authorizes or directs
anything to be done in contravention of Section 3 or 4 is liable on summary
conviction on a first offence to a minimum fine of $1,000.00 and a maximum fine
of $2,000.00; on a second offence to a minimum fine of $2,000.00 and a maximum
fine of $5,000.00; on a third offence to a minimum fine of $5,000.00 and a
maximum fine of $10,000.00. In addition to payment of a fine, the Court may in
each case direct payment of costs and may direct that in default of payment of
the fine, the person being imprisoned for a period not exceeding 6 months.

November 11th Qosing By-law is repealed.

By-law is repealed.

third reading.
